item.title: Mutiny on the Leslie Rae (1987): Murder Aboard a Florida Shrimp Boat
item.description: In July 1987, more than 20 miles off Cape Canaveral, a routine shrimping trip aboard the Leslie Rae turned deadly. A violent mutiny left the captain dead and a first mate fighting for survival in the open Atlantic. Nearly four decades later, it remains one of Florida’s most chilling maritime crime stories. 🌊 The post Mutiny on the Leslie Rae (1987): Murder Aboard a Florida Shrimp Boat first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: The Water Haul: A Useful Cast to Master
item.description: In saltwater fly fishing a long (50-plus feet) accurate cast is often required to be successful at catching fish. This cast is called the double haul. The double haul is a wonderful cast once mastered and will make it possible for the fly angler to not only cast his or her fly to greater distances but also help when casting into the wind. The post The Water Haul: A Useful Cast to Master first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Largemouth Bass Heaven in Lake Okeechobee
item.description: Lake Okeechobee isn’t just a lake — it’s bucket-list bass fishing at its finest. 💥 From trophy largemouth to incredible wildlife and nonstop action, the “Big O” continues to deliver some of the best fishing in the country. item.title: In Winter Get Out of the Boat and Rip Some Lips
item.description: Winter on Florida’s west coast means crystal-clear flats and prime sight-fishing. Step out of the boat, wade quietly, and get within casting range before fish even know you’re there. Leave the trolling motor behind, walk the flats, and go rip some lips. The post In Winter Get Out of the Boat and Rip Some Lips first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Costa Rica’s West Coast: World-Class Sailfish & Marlin Action
item.description: Costa Rica’s Pacific coast is calling! From acrobatic Pacific sailfish to monster blue marlin, the offshore action out of Los Sueños Marina is nothing short of world-class. Calm seas, multiple hookups, and the chance at a 700+ lb marlin make every trip unforgettable. Top it off with fresh dorado at Marina Village and a sunset over Herradura Bay—doesn’t get much better than that. item.title: Armed and Dangerous: Choosing the Right Fishing Rod for Saltwater Success
item.description: The right fishing rod can be the difference between landing a trophy and losing it boatside. Longer rods help control fish from a boat, while shorter rods shine for precision casting while wading. And don’t forget backbone — that lower rod strength is what wins battles when big fish start shaking. Today’s custom saltwater rods are lighter, stronger, and built to handle tough conditions and braided line. Bottom line? There’s no “perfect” rod — just the one that fits your style. item.title: Moosehead Lake: A True Gem in a State of Scenic Wonders
item.description: Moosehead Lake in Maine is a beautiful lake, spanning 74,890 acres with a maximum depth of 246 feet. It is between 35 and 40 miles long and between 2 and 10 miles wide, depending on where you are in the lake. It has a shoreline of 400 miles. It is the largest mountain lake in the eastern United States. The post Moosehead Lake: A True Gem in a State of Scenic Wonders first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.
